content.text: No machine or device converts energy perfectly. Some energy is always "wasted," usually as heat. Efficiency tells us how good a device is at converting input energy into useful output energy. Higher efficiency means less waste.
Efficiency is the ratio of useful output energy to total input energy. It is always less than 1 (or 100%) because some energy is always dissipated, usually as thermal energy.
is the ratio of useful output energy (or power) to total input energy (or power).
Expressed as a decimal (0 to 1) or percentage (0% to 100%)
No device can be more than 100% efficient (conservation of energy)
The wasted energy is usually transferred to thermal energy in the surroundings (dissipated).

items.title: Efficiency (Energy)
bullets: Efficiency = Useful output energy / Total input energy

items.title: Efficiency (Power)
bullets: Efficiency = Useful output power / Total input power
Same formula, just using power instead of energy

items.title: Finding Useful Output
bullets: Useful output = Efficiency x Total input

items.title: Finding Wasted Energy
bullets: Or: Wasted = (1 - Efficiency) x Total input

When energy passes through multiple stages:
When calculating overall efficiency for multiple stages, multiply the individual efficiencies as decimals. The overall efficiency will always be lower than the lowest individual stage efficiency.

Electric car needs 58.8 kJ; petrol car needs 200 kJ

— Electric: input = 50 / 0.85 = 58.8 kJ. Petrol: input = 50 / 0.25 = 200 kJ. The petrol car requires 3.4 times more energy from its source than the electric car for the same useful kinetic energy output. (comparison)
